lead.title: A single step is all you need: ROMS-IMLE hits FID 2.56 on ImageNet without iterative denoising
lead.summary: For years the field assumed competitive generative modeling required many denoising steps. ROMS-IMLE politely disagrees: pair IMLE training with a modest convolutional network and you get FID 2.56 on ImageNet 256 in one shot, with precision and recall intact. If this holds up, the sampling-cost advantage of diffusion stops being a law of nature and becomes an engineering choice — with big implications for latency-bound image and video systems.

top_stories.title: Nvidia's Rubin chips are shipping — the next hardware cycle has officially begun
top_stories.summary: Rubin enters full production and reaches customers, reasserting Nvidia's cadence just as AMD and Broadcom press in. The quiet question underneath: does more efficient modeling eventually shrink demand for all this silicon?

top_stories.title: Moonshot AI chases a $50B valuation ahead of IPO
top_stories.summary: The Kimi K3 developer is reportedly in pre-IPO talks at a ~$50B mark — a signal that China's open-weight frontier is being priced as a first-class geopolitical asset, not a fast follower.

items.title: Mage-Flow: 1024px images in 0.59 seconds on a single A100
items.summary: A 4B-parameter stack — lightweight Mage-VAE tokenizer plus a native-resolution rectified-flow DiT — generates full-res images in under a second and edits in just over one. Efficiency work like this is where diffusion research actually pays rent.

items.title: GEAR: reward the evidence, penalize the distractors
items.summary: A simple RL reward-shaping idea — grounding rewards for key evidence, penalties for irrelevant context — buys +4.6 average points on long-context reasoning, with the largest gains at the longest contexts. Cheap, general, and immediately usable.

items.title: CodeRescue: knowing when to escalate is a routing problem
items.summary: Post-failure recovery for coding agents, formalized: a supervised router plus Conformal Risk Control beats always-escalate solve rates while spending only 35% of its recovery budget. Agent reliability is quietly becoming an engineering discipline.

items.title: GAMUT: frontier models top out at 58.7% on factual completeness
items.summary: Meta's two-level meta-rubric benchmark, spanning 1,813 questions across 10 domains, shows even Gemini 3.1 Pro leaves nearly half the facts on the table. A useful antidote to benchmark saturation narratives.

items.title: AdaFlash: adaptive diffusion drafters lift speculative decoding throughput by 66%
items.summary: On-policy distillation plus an adaptive length head tames the variance in diffusion drafters, delivering up to 66% higher throughput under high concurrency — the regime that actually matters in production serving.

items.title: Google ships a Gemini trio: 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and a security-hardened Flash Cyber
items.summary: Three models, three tradeoffs — speed, cost, and enterprise security. Notably, Gemini's lineup now reads like a pricing page, which tells you exactly where the competitive frontier has moved.

items.title: Poolside's Laguna S 2.1: a 118B MoE coding model with only 8B active parameters
items.summary: Frontier-class agentic coding with 1M context, plus a 33B XS variant aimed at on-device use. Sparse activation keeps making 'big model quality, small model bill' a real product category.

items.title: Jack Dorsey's Buzz wants to be Slack, Notion, and GitHub at once
items.summary: Team chat, built-in AI agents, and Git hosting in one workspace. Ambitious — and the AI-agent layer is the interesting bet, not the chat.

items.title: Computable turns GPU time into a weekly commodity market
items.summary: Buy, sell, and redeem compute by the calendar week with instant liquidity. If compute is the new oil, someone was always going to build the futures exchange.

items.title: Humanoid raises $152M Series A at a $1.35B valuation
items.summary: Another nine-figure round for humanoid robotics — capital keeps arriving ahead of deployments. Watch whether the next twelve months produce revenue or just better demos.

items.title: SkyPilot raises $20M to be the Switzerland of AI compute
items.summary: A Databricks cofounder's orchestration layer that lets teams shop across clouds. Neutrality is a strong pitch — until the clouds decide they'd rather not be shopped.

items.title: Uniti AI raises $12M to put agents in charge of real estate workflows
items.summary: Sales, leasing, and operations agents for property managers, backed by Pathlight Ventures and MetaProp. Vertical agent plays keep getting funded where the workflows are painfully manual.

items.title: Bloomberg: Rubin's arrival reframes the AI hardware race
items.summary: Bloomberg Technology on what full-production Rubin means for Nvidia's moat — and why efficiency gains in models are the bear case hanging over the whole chip cycle.

items.title: Bessemer's Dholakia: Kimi K3 is forcing the US-China AI conversation to grow up
items.summary: On Bloomberg Tech, the case that Chinese open-weight models are genuinely closing on OpenAI and Anthropic — and that the investment cycle is still early, not late.
